concept: MLX thread-local streams and cross-thread lazy array evaluation crashes
summary: MLX issue 2133 (opened 2025-04-28 by awni) tracked three thread-safety items: StreamContext sets the global default stream, the compile cache needs thread safety (issue 2086), and eval of independent graphs is not thread safe (issue 2067).

facts.text: MLX issue 2133 (opened 2025-04-28 by awni) tracked three thread-safety items: StreamContext sets the global default stream, the compile cache needs thread safety (issue 2086), and eval of independent graphs is not thread safe (issue 2067).
zcbenz closed issue 2133 on 2026-04-23, stating MLX has thread-safety support in 0.31.2.
A vllm-mlx user in issue 2133 reported the abort `-[_MTLCommandBuffer addCompletedHandler:]: failed assertion 'Completed handler provided after commit call'` during a 46,831-token prefill.

Issue 3078 reported on MLX 0.30.3 that two threads using `StreamContext` race on the global `Scheduler::default_streams_` unordered_map, and that two threads on the default stream race on `DeviceStream::buffer` and `encoder`.
The 3078 reporter saw `Scheduled handler provided after commit call` and `A command encoder is already encoding to this command buffer`.
awni's answer on 2026-01-29 was to use `with mx.stream(stream_1)` and `with mx.stream(stream_2)` blocks and one combined `mx.eval`, or multiple processes.
zcbenz described five thread-safety levels and judged sharing one stream across threads (level 1) as disastrous without redesigning the command encoder.

zcbenz named "arrays can be evaluated in any thread but cannot depend on each other across threads" (level 2-ii) as the ideal target and said a thread-local default stream matches how the CUDA backend handles the current device.

zcbenz's step list for level 2-ii: move unsafe `Device` methods to `DeviceStream`, optionally merge `DeviceStream` into `CommandEncoder`, make `get_command_encoder` thread safe via a thread-local static, make `Event` and `Fence` creation thread safe without locks, and keep `eval` free of shared global state.

A commenter proposed making `get_command_encoder` create an encoder on demand instead of throwing `There is no Stream(gpu, N) in current thread`, because module-level streams created on another thread leave arrays pointing at unregistered streams.

oMLX issue 1558 gives the stack for the crash: `mlx::core::metal::get_command_encoder` called from `gpu::eval` from `array::eval` from `PyMemoryView_FromObject` in `_extract_tensor_bytes` of `omlx/cache/paged_ssd_cache.py`.
The reporter's proposed fix changes `mx.async_eval(*pre_eval_arrays)` to `mx.eval(*pre_eval_arrays)` under the generation stream so the worker thread does a pure CPU copy.
A second oMLX reporter on 0.3.8 to 0.3.12 saw exit code -6 at 50K to 140K context with Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 models and later struck out an Activity Monitor theory.
Lazy-array handles passed to a worker thread must be materialized with `mx.eval` on the owning thread first, or the worker's implicit eval can crash the process.
